title: 2000 AMC 12 Problem 19
statement: In triangle \(ABC,\) \(AB = 13,\) \(BC = 14,\) and \(AC = 15.\) Let \(D\) denote the midpoint of \(\overline{BC}\) and let \(E\) denote the intersection of \(\overline{BC}\) with the bisector of angle \(BAC.\) Which of the following is closest to the area of triangle \(ADE?\)

solutions.text:
By Heron’s formula, the area of \(\triangle ABC\) is \(\sqrt{21 \cdot 8 \cdot 7 \cdot 6} = 84,\) so the altitude from \(A\) to \(BC\) is \(\dfrac{2 \cdot 84}{14} = 12.\)

The midpoint \(D\) is \(7\) from \(B.\) The bisector from \(A\) meets \(BC\) at \(E\) with \(BE : EC = AB : AC = 13 : 15,\) so \(BE = 14 \cdot \dfrac{13}{28} = 6.5.\)

Both \(D\) and \(E\) lie on \(BC,\) so \(\triangle ADE\) has base \(DE = 7 - 6.5 = 0.5\) and altitude \(12,\) giving area \[ \tfrac12 \cdot 0.5 \cdot 12 = 3. \]

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: By Heron’s formula the area of \(\triangle ABC\) is \(84,\) so the altitude from \(A\) to \(BC\) is \(12\)
\(D\) is at distance \(7\) from \(B\); the bisector foot \(E\) satisfies \(BE : EC = 13 : 15\)
